questions.q: Define solution, solute and solvent, and explain solubility and saturation.

answer.text: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances. The solute is the substance that dissolves, usually present in the smaller amount, such as sugar, and the solvent is the substance in which it dissolves, usually the larger amount, such as water. Water dissolves so many substances that it is called the universal solvent.
Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that can dissolve in a given solvent at a given temperature.

An unsaturated solution can dissolve more solute; a saturated solution can dissolve no more at that temperature. Heating usually lets more of a solid dissolve, while gases dissolve better in cold water.
